change_summary: The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor. The withdrawal is because the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and the notice says the reported results cannot be relied on. The full text and PDF have been replaced by the withdrawal statement. The stored paper's headline result, a 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats, is a result of this kind.
evaluation: In Methods (2.2) your draft sets the green-roof cooling effect to 2.1 °C and cites Okafor et al. [14] as the source of the measured reduction. The stored paper reports that 2.1 °C lower mean daily peak indoor temperature in green-roofed flats. The paper has been withdrawn at the editor's request because the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and the notice says the reported results cannot be relied on. Your Discussion says the green-roof result scales almost directly with that 2.1 °C value taken from [14], and your Conclusions say the result depends strongly on the assumed cooling effect. Both uses are affected and the impact is high: the key parameter of your model comes from the withdrawn paper.
recommendation: The paper has been withdrawn at the request of the editor because the indoor temperature records had been processed with an incorrect sensor calibration, and the notice says the reported results cannot be relied on. In Methods (2.2) the draft sets the green-roof indoor cooling effect to 2.1 °C and cites Okafor et al. [14] as the source of the measured reduction in daily peak indoor temperature. Stop and raise this with your co-authors or supervisor, because the model parameter rests on the withdrawn paper and editing the text will not fix it. In the Discussion the draft says its green-roof result scales almost directly with the 2.1 °C reduction in peak indoor temperature that it takes from Okafor et al. [14]. Then re-check the Discussion and Conclusions and replace or remove the citation.
